source: Rast, L. 2008. 'Large Ruminant Health', ACIAR AH 2005/086 workshop slides, University of Sydney (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com)
text: This overview groups cattle/buffalo disease into four causes: infectious (virus, bacteria, occasionally fungus), parasitic (internal -- worms, liver fluke, blood parasites; external -- ticks, flies, lice), metabolic-deficiency, and poisoning (chemical or plant). It frames the consequence for farmers simply as production loss and income loss, whether the disease stays sub-clinical (no visible signs), causes illness followed by recovery and immunity (as with FMD), or causes illness followed by death (as with HS) -- with some diseases (anthrax, rabies) also posing a risk to human health. Infectious diseases multiply and spread quickly within a herd or village, can be prevented by vaccination, but are difficult and expensive to treat once established (no medication exists for viral disease, and treating many animals is costly and often comes too late).
